Horizon Guest House.blurb: Four-suite B&B on 40 acres of pasture on Mauna Loa's slope above Hōnaunau, with an ocean-view pool.

Don's Mai Tai Bar.blurb: Oceanfront bar at the Royal Kona Resort in Kailua-Kona.
Don's Mai Tai Bar.q: Don's Mai Tai Bar, Royal Kona Resort

Makāula-ʻOʻoma Trail.blurb: Upland forest above Kona — the trip's first birding walk.

Kuleana Rum Shack.blurb: Kuleana Rum Works' restaurant and bar at Queens' MarketPlace, Waikoloa — rum flights and ahi poke.

Puʻukoholā Heiau.blurb: Temple built by Kamehameha I in 1790–91; a prophecy said building it would let him unite the islands.

Puakō Petroglyphs.blurb: Thousands of petroglyphs carved into pāhoehoe lava, a short walk from Holoholokai Beach Park.

Kalahuipuaʻa fishponds.blurb: Ancient Hawaiian fishponds on the Mauna Lani shoreline — the sunset stop before dinner.

CanoeHouse.blurb: Oceanfront restaurant at Mauna Lani, open since 1989.

Hula Daddy.blurb: 100% Kona coffee farm and tasting room in upcountry Holualoa.

Drive to Waimea.blurb: Climbing from the Kona side up into Waimea's ranch country.

Paniolo Adventures.blurb: Horseback rides on a working ranch in the Kohala Mountains.

Kohala Mountain Road.blurb: Highway 250 between Hāwī and Waimea, through ranch land along the Kohala Mountains.

Merriman's.blurb: Peter Merriman's Waimea flagship, a pioneer of Hawaiʻi Regional Cuisine.

Kealakekua Bay.blurb: Marine life conservation district and snorkel spot, home to the Captain Cook monument.

Noio.blurb: 12-seat omakase counter at the Four Seasons Hualālai.

South Point.blurb: Ka Lae — the southernmost point of the United States.

Volcano Village Lodge.blurb: Rainforest lodge in Volcano Village, just outside the national park.

Mauna Kea visitor station.blurb: Visitor station at about 9,200 ft on Mauna Kea — stargazing after the summit.

Mauna Kea summit.blurb: 13,803 ft summit ringed by observatories — sunset above the clouds.

Kīlauea caldera.blurb: Kīlauea's summit caldera and Halemaʻumaʻu crater, in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park.

Volcano House.blurb: Historic hotel on the rim of Kīlauea caldera — lunch with a crater view.

Volcano.blurb: Volcano Village and the ʻōhiʻa rainforest around it.

Puʻu ʻŌʻō Trail.blurb: Saddle Road trail through native-forest kīpuka — birding with Jack Jeffrey.

Palila Discovery Trail.blurb: Māmane forest on Mauna Kea's slope, habitat of the endangered palila.

Lehua Restaurant.blurb: Restaurant in the ʻImiloa Astronomy Center on the UH Hilo campus.

Chain of Craters Road.blurb: Road from Kīlauea's summit down to the sea across decades of lava flows.

Hōlei Sea Arch.blurb: Lava sea arch at the end of Chain of Craters Road.

ʻAkaka Falls.blurb: 442-ft waterfall in ʻAkaka Falls State Park near Honomū.

Hawaiʻi Tropical Botanical Garden.blurb: Rainforest garden in a valley on the Onomea Bay coast, north of Hilo.

The Seaside.blurb: Hilo seafood restaurant on a 30-acre fishpond, run by the Nakagawa family since the 1920s.
The Seaside.q: The Seaside Restaurant and Aqua Farm, Hilo

Royal Hawaiian.blurb: The "Pink Palace of the Pacific", on Waikīkī Beach since 1927.

Mai Tai Bar.blurb: The Royal Hawaiian's oceanfront bar, steps from the sand.

natuRe.blurb: Farm-to-table French tasting menus in Waikīkī.

Bishop Museum.blurb: Hawaiʻi's museum of natural and cultural history, founded in 1889.

La Mariana Sailing Club.blurb: Old-school tiki bar at a Keʻehi Lagoon marina.

Skull & Crown Trading Co..blurb: Horror-tinged Chinatown tiki bar with one of the biggest rum collections in the islands.

ʻAiea Loop Trail.blurb: Ridge loop in Keaīwa Heiau State Recreation Area — the ʻamakihi / ʻelepaio hunt.

Nuʻuanu Pali Lookout.blurb: Windward cliffs where Kamehameha's forces won the 1795 Battle of Nuʻuanu.

Puʻu ʻUalakaʻa.blurb: State wayside on Round Top, looking across Honolulu to Diamond Head.

House Without A Key.blurb: The Halekulani's oceanfront terrace, with hula under the kiawe tree at sunset.

Hanauma Bay.blurb: Nature preserve in a volcanic crater — Oʻahu's best-known snorkeling bay.

Lānaʻi Lookout.blurb: Lookout on the Kaʻiwi coast; on clear days you can see Lānaʻi and Molokaʻi.

Aliʻi Fish Market.blurb: Poke counter on South King Street in Mōʻiliʻili. Bomb poke.

ʻIolani Palace.blurb: Home of Hawaiʻi's last monarchs, King Kalākaua and Queen Liliʻuokalani; completed in 1882.

Michel's at the Colony Surf.blurb: Classic French dining on the water at the foot of Diamond Head.

Kaʻena Point.blurb: Oʻahu's remote western tip — a natural area reserve with nesting seabirds and Hawaiian monk seals.

Kawainui Marsh.blurb: Hawaiʻi's largest remaining wetland, on the edge of Kailua — home to endangered waterbirds.

Azure.blurb: The Royal Hawaiian's beachfront fine-dining restaurant.

Waikīkī Aquarium.blurb: The second-oldest public aquarium in the US, opened in 1904.
